original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Searching below C=40 in the #2017 Eisenstein binary scalar-rectangle or fixed-support block-linear additive pairing model; specify a changed premise instead. This bound does not cover every complex decoder.

actual_scope: On the selected per-call profile {1:2412, 2:418, 3:432, 4:142, 5:82, 8:8}, replace the eight rank-8 private-temporary copy children by four rank-16 block children, preserving their paid mass 64 and leaving every other profile count, the 64-per-call centre charge, 73/896/9 template, one unpaid coordinate and halving guard unchanged. Assume zero additional gathering, copying, frame, restoration, hosting or precision cost, then compute the exact ceiling interval and relative gain.
scope_change_reason: The card calls for a small exact identity after an optimistic profile screen. This run narrows the first screen to the only existing rank-8 copy mass: pair all eight rank-8 children into four rank-16 block climbs at zero added cost. The favorable exact ceiling already misses the 5% gate, so no synthesis or decoder identity search was justified for this subroute.
bottleneck_link: The catalogue requires at least a 5% ceiling gain from a rank-shape candidate. This screen changes only 64 of 5,586 local paid mass and gives an exact zero-overhead upper gain below 0.212%; it rejects this copy-only block route before synthesis, without ruling out larger changes to rank-1 through rank-5 children.
stop_rule: Recompute the selected profile and the single rank-8-to-rank-16 replacement with the pinned exact ceiling engine at grid 1e-12. Stop this candidate if the conservative relative-gain upper endpoint is below 1/20. Do not generalize to other ranks, block identities, words, or changed coverage.
evidence: CERTIFICATE.json records both certified ceiling brackets, the conservative relative-gain interval [1190479/563351370, 3571439/1690054109], the unchanged paid mass 5,586, the moved mass 64 and the strict comparison 3571439/1690054109 < 1/20. verify.py recomputes the brackets from the pinned ceiling.py and checks a baseline, full-rank-16 ideal sensitivity, and an extra-charge negative control.

open_questions.question: Can a distinct block-frame identity reorganize a substantial part of the rank-1 through rank-5 mass into larger-rank children while preserving the selected local operator?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The zero-overhead copy-only grouping changes too little mass to approach the card threshold, while the all-mass rank-16 relaxation has a large ideal ceiling gain. A broader identity is the remaining route within this task that could matter.
open_questions.first_step: For a fresh selector seed, name one explicit chronological block and its source/target frames, count every copied direction and restoration, and screen its complete profile before synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: No concrete identity presently maps the rank-1 through rank-5 portions of the pinned local word into one rank-16 recursive child; the copy-only screen does not address them.

selected_method: Evaluate a zero-overhead block-climb relaxation that replaces the selected word's eight rank-8 private-temporary copy children by four rank-16 children, leaving the rest of the local profile, centre charge, coverage law and guard unchanged.
claim_status: No advance claim posted; this is a bounded exact screening result, not a construction or reservation.
